title: G 63 AMG
verdict: The last G 63 built on the old W463 body: a 5.5-litre biturbo V8, three lockers and solid axles. It's the quickest way to make a 1979 truck feel modern. Hard-used examples are cheaper than you'd expect, and an M157 that has missed its maintenance costs more than you'd expect.

paragraphs: The G 63 AMG replaced the supercharged [[g-class/g55-amg|G 55 AMG]] in 2012 and reached American showrooms that August as a 2013 model. It ran until the 2018 model year, the last before the redesigned [[g-class/second-gen|second-generation G]]. It uses AMG's 5.5-litre biturbo V8 and a seven-speed automatic, and it was the first AMG G with neither a supercharger nor a five-speed. The [[g-class/w463|W463]] underneath is unchanged: ladder frame, solid axles on coils, a two-speed transfer case and three locking differentials. AMG gave the truck a much bigger engine and left the off-road hardware alone.

story.heading: TURBOS REPLACE THE SUPERCHARGER
paragraphs: Mercedes revealed the G 63 and the V12 G 65 in April 2012, ahead of the Beijing show. The M157 V8 displaces 5,461 cc and makes 544 PS with 760 Nm (560 lb-ft) from 2,000 rpm. Mercedes quoted 0–60 mph in 5.3 seconds and a 130 mph limiter, and claimed 13 per cent lower fuel consumption on the European cycle than the G 55. The engine drives an AMG SPEEDSHIFT PLUS 7G-TRONIC with three modes, automatic throttle blips on downshifts and ECO start/stop.

The rest of the update came from the 2012 G-Class refresh. The dashboard and centre console came from the ML, and the truck gained a colour TFT instrument cluster, a tablet-style COMAND screen, DISTRONIC PLUS, Blind Spot Assist and LED daytime running lights. AMG added a twin-blade grille, a bumper with three large intakes, six-piston front calipers from the ML 63 on 14.8-inch discs, and 20-inch wheels on 275/50 R20 tyres. AutoGuide priced a 2013 US truck at $134,300, about $20,000 more than a [[g-class/g550|G 550]].

story.heading: WHY OFF-ROADERS SHOULD CARE
paragraphs: In the bodywork that matters off-road, a G 63 is the same truck as a G 550. Kelley Blue Book listed a 36-degree approach angle and a 7,716 lb tow rating. MotorTrend gave 27 degrees of departure, 21 degrees of breakover, about 8 inches of ground clearance and 24 inches of wading depth. It still has a low-range transfer case and centre, rear and front locks controlled by dashboard buttons. The off-road weak points are AMG's own choices: low-profile 20s, a side exhaust that exits ahead of the rear wheels, and huge front brakes that limit which wheels will fit.

Buyers liked it. MotorTrend reported in late 2013 that the G 63 had become the best-selling AMG product in the US. That's why so many are on the used market. Most owners drove them on pavement, so the lockers on a typical used truck have rarely been used.

story.heading: 2016 UPDATE AND THE END
paragraphs: For the 2016 model year the truck was renamed Mercedes-AMG G 63. Output rose by 27 PS to 571 PS (563 hp), with torque unchanged at 760 Nm and 0–100 km/h in 5.4 seconds. All G-Class models got new shock absorbers, revised ASR and ABS calibration, new bumpers and new instrument dials. AMG also offered an Edition 463 package with 21-inch wheels and a stainless underguard, and a colour package with bright paints such as alien green and sunset beam. The G 550 switched to the 4.0-litre twin-turbo M176 at the same time, and the [[g-class/4x4-squared|4×4²]] followed in 2015 on a shortened chassis from the [[g-class/g63-6x6|G 63 AMG 6×6]], AMG's six-wheeler derived from the Australian Army's [[g-class/w461|W461]]-family truck.

The 2018 model year was the last for this body in the US. Its successor kept the G 63 name but moved to the twin-turbo 4.0-litre M177 and independent front suspension. That makes the 2013–2018 truck the last AMG G with a solid front axle. On Bring a Trailer it has also become the cheapest way into a biturbo AMG G: from 2025 to October 2026, the median sale was about $65,500.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · 2013–15 OR 2016–18?
callout.title: Pre- and post-facelift G 63s
paragraphs: The 2013–2015 trucks have 544 PS (Mercedes USA quoted 544 hp) and the original dampers. The 2016–2018 trucks have 571 PS (563 hp), new shocks, updated ESP and ABS calibration and revised gauges. Torque, the seven-speed and the three lockers are the same throughout. EPA ratings barely change: 12 mpg city and 14 highway every year, with 2018 rated 15 highway.

In 2025–26 Bring a Trailer sales, 2013–15 G 63s had a median of about $61,000 and 2016–18 trucks about $76,750. A buyer who plans to lift the truck and fit tyres gets little extra off-road from the newer trucks. The extra money mostly buys lower mileage, newer electronics and recall work that's more likely to have been done.

engineering_intro: Under the AMG trim, the G 63 is still a W463. The body sits on a separate ladder frame, both axles are solid and coil-sprung, a two-speed transfer case drives all four wheels permanently, and three dashboard switches lock the centre, rear and front differentials. AMG changed the engine, gearbox, brakes, exhaust, wheels and damper settings.

engineering.note: Long-wheelbase five-door body; AMG flares, running boards and side-exit exhaust.
Coil springs on link-located beam axles. This is the last AMG G before the 2019 switch to independent front suspension.
Three 100% locks and low range, as on every W463.
5,461 cc, direct injection; 544 PS / 760 Nm, 571 PS from 2016.
AMG SPEEDSHIFT PLUS calibration, three modes, ECO start/stop.
ML 63 calipers on 14.8 × 1.42 in front discs; they rule out most 18-inch wheels.

engineering_note.title: TWO COOLING CIRCUITS
engineering_note.body: The M157 has a main engine circuit and a separate low-temperature charge-air circuit. AMSOIL lists capacities of 14.6 qt and 3.1 qt. Both circuits rely on plastic fittings and hoses next to very hot turbos. FCP Euro sells a turbo coolant-line kit for this engine because those lines are a common failure, and a split line can empty the system quickly. Check both reservoirs before every trail run.

generations_table.note: Three portal axles, five lockers; about 100 built
US MY2016–2018; new dampers, revised ASR/ABS

buying_checks.head: Is it really a G 63?
buying_checks.body: Many G 550s have been fitted with AMG bumpers, grilles and badges. US G 63 VINs from Bring a Trailer listings begin WDCYC7DF (2013–2016) and WDCYC7DH (2018). A same-era G 550 reads WDCYC3HF. Check the VIN and data card, not the bodywork.

buying_checks.head: Recall paperwork
buying_checks.body: Make sure NHTSA 17V250 (steering coupling, 2013–2016) has been done. On 2016–17 trucks, also check 17V713 (ESP with DISTRONIC PLUS). Run the VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup before you hand over money.

buying_checks.head: Oil consumption and misfires
buying_checks.body: Ask how much oil it uses between services and scan for stored codes. The M157 can suffer cylinder scoring at higher mileage. Misfires are often plugs, coils or oil-soaked cam-magnet connectors, but persistent misfires or consumption justify a borescope before purchase.

buying_checks.head: Coolant around the turbos
buying_checks.body: Look for coolant crust or a sweet smell around the turbos and the lines that feed them, and check both coolant reservoirs. MBWorld owners report cracked turbo coolant lines, and a pressure test is cheap.

buying_checks.head: Oil at the cam magnets
buying_checks.body: Unplug a camshaft-adjuster magnet connector. If there's oil inside, it is wicking into the harness, and the magnets need replacing with sacrificial pigtails fitted.

buying_checks.head: Seals under the truck
buying_checks.body: Check for gear oil on the inside of the front wheels and on the big AMG calipers (front axle seals), at the transfer-case outputs and at the pinion seals. An MBWorld member says pinion seal leaks are 'very common around 60k–80k'.

buying_checks.head: Test all three lockers
buying_checks.body: Engage centre, rear and front in order on loose ground and watch the indicators. A truck that has only ever been driven on pavement can have lockers that don't engage.

buying_checks.head: Rust and drains
buying_checks.body: Check the tailgate's lower edge, door bottoms, sills, rear frame tubes and spring mounts. A G 63 rusts like any other G, and 20-inch wheels don't stop road salt.

repairs.title: Spark plugs & ignition coils (M157)
repairs.symptoms: Misfire codes (P0300-series), rough idle, hesitation under boost. Often the plugs' age is simply unknown.
repairs.fix: Remove the engine covers and intake trim, pull each coil, and replace all eight plugs with Mercedes-spec plugs torqued to the service manual figure. Euro Premium Parts' M157 guide recommends inspecting or replacing the coils at the same time, at about 40,000–50,000 miles. Before replacing a coil, check its connector and boot for oil.
repairs.tools: Thin-wall spark plug socket · extensions and swivel · torque wrench · dielectric grease

repairs.title: Camshaft-adjuster magnets leaking oil
repairs.symptoms: Oil inside the four camshaft-adjuster magnet connectors at the front of the heads. Possible cam-timing codes. On neglected engines, oil wicks along the harness toward the engine computer.
repairs.fix: Replace all four magnets. Fit sacrificial wiring pigtails so any future leak stops at a cheap connector. Clean the harness plugs with electronic cleaner and check the far end of the harness for oil. FCP Euro's kit is built for this job on the M157, M278 and related engines.
repairs.tools: Torx bits · electrical contact cleaner · rags · magnets and pigtails

repairs.title: Turbo coolant lines & water pump
repairs.symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious puddle, coolant crust or a sweet smell near the turbos, low-coolant warning, overheating. An MBWorld owner of a 2014 G 63 found a cracked coolant line at the driver-side turbo.
repairs.fix: Pressure-test the system to find the leak. Replace the turbo coolant feed and return lines as a set, and on a high-mileage engine do the water pump and thermostat housing at the same time. FCP Euro calls the lines 'a common failure item that can lead to coolant loss and engine overheating.' Access is tight. MBWorld owners disagree on whether it's a sensible DIY, so plan to remove intake parts.
repairs.tools: Cooling-system pressure tester · hose-clamp pliers · flare and line wrenches · MB 325.6 coolant · vacuum fill tool helpful

repairs.title: 7G-TRONIC fluid & filter service
repairs.symptoms: Harsh or delayed shifts, flare between gears, or just no service record. FCP Euro notes that the 722.9's most common failures are electronic.
repairs.fix: Drain the pan and the torque converter, replace the filter and pan gasket, refill with MB 236.15 ATF and set the level at the specified fluid temperature with a scan tool. AMSOIL lists the 722.9 total fill as 9.5 qt, and a drain-and-fill replaces only part of it. If shifts are erratic, have a scan tool read the gearbox fault codes before replacing parts.
repairs.tools: Scan tool for ATF temperature · fluid pump · torque wrench · new filter, gasket and plugs

repairs.title: Front axle seal leak
repairs.symptoms: Gear oil on the inner front wheels or the six-piston calipers, a gear-oil smell, brakes pulling.
repairs.fix: Replace both front axle seals and inspect the shafts for scoring. Replace contaminated pads and resurface or replace the rotors. au7o lists this leak for G 63s and rates it critical because the oil ends up on the brakes.
repairs.tools: Seal puller and driver · hub tools · GL-5 gear oil · brake parts if oil-soaked

repairs.title: Pinion & transfer-case seal leaks
repairs.symptoms: Oil drips at the front of either differential or at the transfer-case outputs; oil spray on the driveshafts.
repairs.fix: First make sure the axle breather tube isn't kinked or blocked, because pressure pushes oil past seals. Pinion seals need care: an MBWorld member notes the pinion bearing preload is set by a crush sleeve, so mark and measure before removing the nut. For transfer-case output seals, refill with Mercedes-approved fluid and check the flanges for wear.
repairs.tools: Flange holding tool · seal puller · inch-pound torque wrench · fluids

repairs.title: Steering damper & front-end wander
repairs.symptoms: Wander, wheel shake at 55–70 mph, vague on-centre feel. au7o reports this as the most common W463 complaint.
repairs.fix: Replace the damper with an OEM or upgraded unit. Check the drag link and tie-rod ends for play and align afterwards. Ask whether recall 17V250 (steering coupling) has been done.
repairs.tools: Sockets and wrenches · tie-rod end puller · alignment afterwards

repairs.title: Frame & body rust treatment
repairs.symptoms: Bubbling at the tailgate lower edge, door bottoms and sills; scale on the rear frame tubes and spring mounts.
repairs.fix: Remove loose scale, treat with a converter, then apply cavity wax inside the frame and doors and an underbody coating. Keep the drain holes clear. Cut out and weld anything perforated.
repairs.tools: Wire wheels · rust converter · cavity-wax wand · underbody coating

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: About 32 inches, on 20-inch wheels. An Expedition Portal owner runs 275/55R20 (about 32 in) on an unlifted G 63, and another 2017 G 63 owner was told by his dealer the size 'will work fine'. Most unlifted W463s fit 33-inch 275/70R18s, but one Expedition Portal member says 18-inch wheels 'will not fit on the G63' over its big front calipers, so try a wheel on the hub before you buy a set. Recode the tyre size so the speedometer and ESP stay accurate.

faq.q: What size are the factory tires?
faq.a: 275/50R20, according to TireSize.com's fitment data for the 2015, 2016 and 2018 G 63. The launch press material lists 9.5 × 20 AMG wheels. The Edition 463 package offered 21-inch wheels.

faq.q: Does it have low range and lockers?
faq.a: Yes. It is a full W463 with permanent four-wheel drive, a low-range transfer case and centre, rear and front locking differentials.
7,716 lb, according to Kelley Blue Book's 2013 G 63 guide. Check your own truck's manual and hitch.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: EPA: 12 mpg city, 14 highway, 13 combined on premium for every model year from 2013 to 2017, with 2018 rated 15 highway. Bigger tyres and a roof rack lower it.

faq.q: What oil does it take, and how much?
faq.a: AMSOIL lists 9 qt with the filter, in 0W-40 or 5W-40 full synthetic meeting Mercedes approval. Euro Premium Parts cites MB 229.5/229.51 and recommends changing it every 10,000 miles or yearly. FCP Euro's G 63 oil kit comes with 9 litres.
faq.src: AMSOIL · EURO PREMIUM PARTS · FCP EURO

faq.a: It's strong when maintained, but neglect gets expensive. The well-documented jobs are spark plugs and coils, oil-leaking cam magnets, turbo coolant lines, and turbo oil feed lines on older engines. Cylinder scoring is the serious risk at higher mileage. Buy on service history and a borescope inspection, not on mileage alone.
faq.src: FCP EURO · EURO PREMIUM PARTS · AU7O

faq.a: Off-road they are the same truck: same frame, axles, transfer case and lockers. The G 63 adds roughly 150 hp, bigger brakes that rule out 18-inch wheels, and a more complicated twin-turbo engine. If you'll mostly drive trails, a G 550 is cheaper to buy and fit with tyres. If you'll mostly drive pavement, the G 63's engine is the reason to buy it.

There's no consensus best year, so buy on condition. 2016–2018 trucks have 563 hp, new dampers and recalibrated ESP and ABS, and they sell for roughly $15,000 more on Bring a Trailer. 2013–2015 trucks are the bargain. Handsome Motors says the M157 in the G 63 got timing-chain and head-bolt updates, and wants the cooling system and water pump inspected on any of them. Whichever year you buy, make sure the steering-coupling recall (17V250, 2013–2016) is done.
faq.src: CARSCOOPS · NHTSA · BRING A TRAILER · HANDSOME MOTORS

faq.q: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
faq.a: No. Locked differentials stop the wheels turning at different speeds, so on grippy surfaces the driveline binds and the tyres scrub. Lock them on loose ground at low speed and unlock before you're back on tarmac.
The second-generation G 63 for the 2019 model year. It has a 4.0-litre twin-turbo M177 with 577 hp, a 40:60 torque split and independent front suspension, and it still has three lockers.

mods.why: Taller, narrower all-terrains on 20s, or smaller wheels that have been test-fitted over the brakes. This is the biggest off-road improvement for a G 63.
A 60–100 mm spring lift with matched dampers makes room for 33–35-inch tyres and controls a heavy V8 nose.
Bolt-on portal conversions that give a pre-2019 W463 4×4²-style clearance without using the factory truck's parts.
